findings.why: In a 'bridal glow' cream ad, 'Removes Tanning' next to 'Brightens Skin' and 'Fades Pigmentation' frames a lighter complexion as the goal, which breaches skin-lightening guidelines. It is also an elimination claim (CLM-04).
findings.fix: Remove it. If kept at all: 'Helps fade the look of dark spots for a more even-looking tone' (only with substantiation).

findings.span: Heaven Magic’s Bridal Super Powerful Cream
findings.why: The ad is marked brand-authored for Minimalist but promotes another brand's product and links to www.heavenmagic.com. Confirm it is in the right account and review queue before anything else.
findings.fix: Remove from the Minimalist review queue, or replace with the correct Minimalist product and URL.

rule_hit_review.why: 'Removes Tanning' is an elimination claim, and in this bridal-cream context it also reads as a fairness claim (raised separately under CLM-06).
'No Harmful Chemicals' is a 'chemical-free'-style safety absolute that implies other products are unsafe.
'No Side Effects' can't be substantiated for every user.
'visible glow in just 7 days' is a time-bound result with no study or qualifier on the ad.
'Start seeing results from the 1st week!' is a time-bound result with no supporting study shown.
'Trusted by 100,000+ Women Across India' is an unsourced social-proof figure.
The second-person question asserts the viewer has dull skin, dark spots or uneven tone.
'Magic' here is part of the brand name 'Heaven Magic', not hype used in the copy, though 'Super Powerful' is.
'unlock your bridal glow' is hype phrasing.
The copy is led by emoji bullets throughout (✅, 💛, 🔥, 🎁, 🛒), a category signature.

tone_read: This reads entirely as a category fairness/bridal cream ad, with an agitation hook, emoji bullets, hype ('Super Powerful', 'unlock') and time-pressure promises. Nothing in it sounds like Minimalist.
language_read: No active, concentration or mechanism is named; it relies on unhedged outcome verbs ('Brightens', 'Fades', 'Removes', 'Evens Out') and safety absolutes. The 'No Harmful Chemicals' framing directly contradicts the brand's stated position.
